root_cause: The scheduled dispatcher path used persistent python.exe/.cmd wrappers and did not reach service progress under Task Scheduler; IgnoreNew and stale wrapper processes prevented later timer ticks.
The scheduler context did not have the N: mapping used by the old wrapper.
Nested per-case schtasks launch was unreliable and the full /TR command exceeded the Windows Task Scheduler command length limit.
Same-attempt reacquisition inserted a second reservation and hit the unique branch/case/attempt constraint.
PowerShell/tasklist process census could hang under pythonw Task Scheduler context.
A stale scientific_entry_boundary.json could be accepted without requiring a new fencing-matched boundary.

answers.why_auto_refill_failed: The old Scheduler/wrapper process model was not progressing reliably, and the path also had a N: mapping dependency, nested schtasks launch, command-length, same-attempt reservation, process-census, and stale-boundary faults.
answers.what_wakes_now: The one-minute APCD_V3_COUPLING_DISPATCHER task wakes a transient pythonw dispatcher service. Each tick rechecks WAIT_RESOURCE_CAPACITY and invokes the native host process when admitted.
answers.controller_restart: PASS via controller_restart_preserves_waiting_case; reopening the DB preserved the same attempt and did not create a duplicate or scientific entry.
answers.one_freed_slot: PASS via multislot_autorefill; the next waiting case is admitted after a slot becomes available.
answers.attempt_identity: attempt_002 is the sole current canonical attempt; attempt_003 was not created.
answers.production_boundary: YES: the formal scheduled-task dispatcher path reached the real preentry boundary automatically for the canonical case, without a manual per-case launch and without solver invocation.
